title: Standard continuation deltas without `id` must still be appended (baseline-correct upstream stream)
source: litellm#20711 (2026-02): upstream stream was standard; the proxy's iterator skipped id-less chunks (`if not call_id_raw: continue`), silently dropping argument deltas after the first chunk
endpointClass: openai (spec-conformant stream; fault class targets client/proxy accumulators)

expected.note: This is what a correct OpenAI stream looks like: id and name only on the first delta, argument fragments on later deltas keyed by index alone. Any accumulator that requires id on continuation chunks (or skips id-less chunks) fails this baseline — the fault lives in the client/proxy layer, not upstream.

failureModeIfBuggy: Source-case proxy dropped fragments after the first chunk: streamed arguments truncated to `{"lo`, then a completion-time consolidation re-inserted the full arguments as one burst — the loss was masked as lag, and finish_reason still said tool_calls, so nothing downstream errored.
mutationHooks: Remove the `index` from continuation deltas — expected must flip to f2-class anomaly, proving the fixture distinguishes 'no id' (normal) from 'no index' (noncompliant).
Swap fragment order — expected.arguments must fail to parse, proving concatenation order is asserted.
specBasis: OpenAI function-calling streaming guide: first chunk carries id and name; subsequent chunks carry argument fragments only (keyed by index) — absence of id on continuations is the documented norm.
Source case confirms upstream (OpenAI/Azure standard format) emitted a conformant stream; the defect was the proxy's accumulation filter.
notes: Fault-layer teaching fixture: same input stream is 'pass' for a correct accumulator and 'silent loss' for an over-strict one. The diagnostic tool must therefore judge the accumulator against the raw events, not merely replay the SDK's own projection (avoid self-as-referee, 0.6.0 plan §4).
